paper_summary: Buddhacosa et al. manufactured epoxy-matrix syntactic foams from West System 105/206 bisphenol A/F epoxy and West System 410 sodium borosilicate hollow glass microspheres by VARTM, partially replacing the microspheres with end-of-life tyre-derived milled crumb rubber particles (250-425 um) at HGM:rubber weight ratios from 1:0 to 1:5. Increasing rubber content raised foam density from 518 to 635 kg/m3, lowered HGM volume fraction from 64 to 50 vol.%, and kept manufacturing void content below 0.5 vol.%. Thermogravimetric analysis (10 and 30 C/min, N2 and air), TGA-FTIR evolved-gas analysis, SEM/EDS and ATR-FTIR char characterisation, cone calorimetry at 35 and 50 kW/m2 and UL94 horizontal-burn tests showed that rubber increased residual char and total heat release, raised the fire growth rate at 35 kW/m2 but lowered it at 50 kW/m2, and reduced the flame spread rate from 81.3 to 45.0 mm/min so that all rubber-reinforced foams achieved a UL94 HB rating.

processing.matrix_name: Bisphenol A/F epoxy resin blend, West System 105, with West System 206 slow hardener (Gougeon Brothers Inc.)
processing.particle_grade: West System 410 Microlight, amorphous sodium borosilicate hollow glass microspheres (HGM)

structure.microstructure_notes: Table 1 composition: epoxy 87.5 wt.% / 35.7 vol.%, HGM 12.5 wt.% / 64.1 vol.%, rubber 0.0 wt.% / 0.0 vol.%, unintended void 0.2 +/- 0.2 vol.%. Measured bulk density 518 +/- 7 kg/m3; total foam porosity (including hollow HGM interiors) 56.8 +/- 1.3 %. Void content (CT, VolMaxStudio) below 0.5 vol.%, far below the 2-10 vol.% typical of stir-cast foam. HGM particle size 32 +/- 23 um, rubber 255 +/- 123 um (Gaussian, optical image analysis, ImageJ). SEM showed debonding/microcracking at the rubber/epoxy interface (chemically unfunctionalised, hydrophobic rubber vs hydrophilic epoxy) but good HGM/epoxy bonding with no interfacial microcracks.

extraction_notes:
On-topic syntactic-foam paper (epoxy matrix + hollow glass microspheres), but it reports NO mechanical properties: no modulus, strength, strain, energy absorption, plateau stress, thermal conductivity, CTE, DMA or moisture uptake are measured for these foams. The measured quantities are physical (density, porosity, void content, phase fractions) plus thermal-degradation (Tmax, residual char), fire-reaction (t_ign, pHRR1/2, THR, heat of combustion, FIGRA) and flame-spread (UL94 elapsed flame time, burning rate, rating) properties, none of which have a field in this schema. Every Properties field is therefore null; the numbers are preserved verbatim in test.specimen_notes and in the per-table evidence items so nothing is lost.
RECORD GRANULARITY: six records are emitted, one per foam composition SYN(1:0) through SYN(1:5). Although the paper reports six test conditions per composition (TGA at 30 C/min in N2, 10 C/min in N2 and 30 C/min in air; cone calorimetry at 35 and 50 kW/m2; UL94), none of those conditions produces a value that maps to a schema property field, so splitting each composition into six records would yield 36 rows that are byte-identical in Processing, Structure and Properties. All six test conditions are instead captured inside each composition's single record.
UNIT CONVERSIONS: measured density kg/m3 -> g/cm3 (e.g. 518 -> 0.518); HGM vol.% and wt.% -> fractions (e.g. 64.1 vol.% -> 0.641); void vol.% -> matrix_porosity_fraction (e.g. 0.2 -> 0.002).
FIELD CHOICES: matrix_porosity_fraction holds the Table 1 'Void' column (unintended VARTM porosity, 0.0-0.3 vol.%), NOT the Table 1 'Porosity' column (47-57 %), which is the total foam porosity including the hollow interiors of the HGM particles; that value is recorded in microstructure_notes to avoid conflating the two. cure_or_process_temperature_c = 60 C, the 8 h post-cure; the 24 h primary cure at ambient 23 C is noted in evidence. particle_true_density_g_cc left null (never stated). particle_wall_thickness_ratio left null (never stated). test.temperature_c left null because the tests are ramped-temperature or radiant-heat-flux exposures with no single test temperature. test_type = 'other' for all records, since none of compression/tension/flexure/shear/impact/dma/fatigue/hydrostatic applies to TGA, cone calorimetry or UL94.
EXCLUDED ROWS: Table 2 also lists the three neat constituents (HGM alone Tmax 228 +/- 3 C, char 63.6 +/- 1.2 %; rubber alone 418 +/- 4 C, 35.9 +/- 0.2 %; epoxy alone 419 +/- 2 C, 8.0 +/- 0.3 %). These are single-phase reference materials, not hollow-particle composites, so no records were created for them. Literature heats of combustion quoted in the discussion (tyre rubber 39-45 MJ/kg, bisphenol resin 31 MJ/kg) are secondary values from refs 36-38 and are not schema properties, so no 'secondary' records were created either. The text states compression strength and modulus of VARTM foam were 'at least 10% higher' than stir-cast foam measured in the authors' laboratories, but gives no absolute numbers, so no modulus or strength value was recorded.
MINOR TEXT INCONSISTENCY: the running text says rubber content increased 'from 10.2 wt.% in SYN(1:1) to 33.5 wt.% in SYN(1:5)'; 10.2 wt.% is the HGM column value and 33.5 wt.% differs slightly from the 33.3 wt.% given in Table 1. Table 1 values were used throughout.
